agent-director-admin is an operator tool. Do not run any of its commands without explicit approval from a human for this specific run. Agents and automated callers must not run it.

# agent-director-admin reference

install.sh installs agent-director-admin at `~/.config/agent-director/admin/agent-director-admin` and never on PATH. Store and configuration requirements are described below for each action.

## Global flags

For kill-finished and delete, use agent-director's store, home and tmux overrides. migrate-journal uses the configured store unless --store-path overrides it. snapshot-store requires an explicit --store-path and loads no config. Each global flag goes before or after the verb, as --flag value or --flag=value.

- `--store-path <path>`: Use <path> instead of the configured store ([store] db_path in ~/.config/agent-director/config.toml, by default ~/.config/agent-director/state.db). Required for snapshot-store, which reads the existing source without opening it through SQLite. With migrate-journal --check-only, enables the read-only holder inventory after argument checks; without it that mode checks arguments only.
- `--home <dir>`: Use <dir> as HOME for this run, so the config, the store and every other ~/ path resolve under it.
- `--tmux-command <path>`: Run <path> as tmux instead of the tmux on PATH.
- `--create-if-missing <true|false>`: For kill-finished and delete: false refuses a missing store (ErrStoreOpen); true or omitted creates its parent directories, file and schema. migrate-journal and snapshot-store require an existing source and never create it.

## snapshot-store

`agent-director-admin --store-path <absolute-path> snapshot-store --directory <private-directory> [--busy-timeout-ms <ms>]`

Copy a consistent database and committed WAL for installer preflight without opening the original through SQLite or changing its files. The directory must exist, be empty and have mode 0700; the caller removes it after reading the snapshot. Read-only POSIX locks guard capture on Linux and macOS; busy, unreadable, changing or unsupported sources refuse with ErrStoreOpen. No config is loaded and no schema is initialized or migrated. Run in a separate process with no other source database descriptors. An error prints one JSON envelope ({err_name, err_description}) on stderr and exits 1.

### Flags

- `--directory <path>`: Absolute path of an existing empty private directory. Required.
- `--busy-timeout-ms <ms>`: Capture and lock-wait budget, in milliseconds, 1 through 2147483647; default 10000.

### Output

{path}: the private state.db snapshot. Read it with SQLite so committed WAL frames are included; the original remains untouched.

## migrate-journal

`agent-director-admin [--store-path <absolute-path>] migrate-journal --maintenance-window --roots-complete --backup-dir <new-absolute-dir> [--legacy-root <absolute-dir>...] [--check-only]`

Cut over the configured store's legacy native-input journals under an operator-maintained maintenance window. Stop incompatible MCP servers, helpers, hooks, commands and launch preparation and prevent new old-runtime invocations through committed verification. A pending schema transition requires an exact authorization sentinel; already-current verification requires none. Invoking HOME's current and old input roots are always included, even for a custom database; declare every additional root. Unreadable inventory refuses without killing processes. SQLite remains authoritative after commit even if file retirement fails. docs/operator-actions.md Upgrading the native-input journal says what to do for each refusal reason, including the direct verification retry after a committed or uncertain refusal. Recovery restores the stopped-writer backup and matching prior binary: later writes are lost; reconcile uncertain attempts before restarting an older runtime. Never reset the schema version or reconstruct replayable journals. With --check-only it makes the argument checks the real run makes first (the window and roots assertions; the backup directory absolute, new and outside every legacy root; legacy roots absolute and clean). With an explicit global --store-path it then runs a process inventory of the current layout (aliases resolved), without the real attempt's owner/mode, link-component or ACL verdicts, refusing old_or_unverified_mutators with the processes to stop. Without --store-path it stays argument-only. Both check-only modes open no store, load no config, take no lock and write nothing. An error prints one JSON envelope on stderr and exits 1: ErrJournalMigrationRefused, ErrInvalidFlags, ErrConfigMalformed or ErrStoreOpen. Its details.cutover says what this attempt committed: not_committed (no cutover commit; details.steps_committed says whether an earlier schema step committed), committed, or unknown (anything else, such as an unconfirmed commit or a migration lock another administrator holds or that cannot be checked); --check-only always reports not_committed. ErrJournalMigrationRefused also carries details.refusal {reason, processes, action} and, from a real run, details.result, whose authority is set when the attempt read it. INT, TERM or HUP before the cutover commit begins stops the attempt with reason interrupted; once that commit has begun, the attempt finishes first; an INT or HUP ignored at start stays ignored. Run it as the agents' user and in their tmux environment.

### Flags

- `--maintenance-window`: Assert that the operator has established and will maintain the admission boundary through verification. Required.
- `--roots-complete`: Assert that every legacy input root relevant to this store identity is established and declared. Required.
- `--legacy-root <absolute-dir>`: Additional legacy input root containing store-id/launch-token directories. Repeatable.
- `--backup-dir <new-absolute-dir>`: Exclusive new directory for the stopped-writer database/WAL/SHM and legacy-evidence backup. Required.
- `--check-only`: Check arguments and, with an explicit global --store-path, run a process inventory of the current layout (aliases resolved), without the real attempt's owner/mode, link-component or ACL verdicts, then exit: {} when clear, ErrJournalMigrationRefused with details.refusal, details.cutover not_committed, details.steps_committed false and no result when refused. No store open, config load, lock or writes.

### Output

{store_id, authority, backup, retirement_pending}; authority sqlite means the committed marker was verified, never permission to restart old mutators. With --check-only, {}.

## kill-finished

`agent-director-admin kill-finished --instance-id <id>`

End a finished row's (ended or missing) own old session, after a human has looked at it. It ends the session only if it reported in to the row: the row records the agent's process id and the session was created, in whole seconds, before the row finished. It ends the agent's pane and the row's labelled session, waits for the agent process (or, when the process cannot be checked, looks the session up once more) and succeeds once the agent process is gone. It also ends this id's own abandoned launch, which resume and spawn --reuse-finished refuse: when the row records a launch token but no tmux server or pane of that launch, the sessions carrying an earlier launch's label of the row's id in this store, once the youngest has run for at least the starting-session bound; such a launch never reports in, so its agent process is the process of the pane that launch created, never one the row records. The row's state and every other field stay unchanged, so the conversation stays resumable. With no session of the row's current launch found, it acts as kill does on a live row. A live row (pending included) is refused with ErrSpawnNotResumable, with no lookup; an unknown id is ErrSpawnNotFound. These refusals send no kill and change nothing: ErrInternal (unusable recorded tmux session name), ErrTmuxUnresponsive (still stopping or still starting: wait and run it again; or tmux did not answer usably), ErrTmuxSessionConflict (never reported in, or conflicting labels), ErrTmuxNotAvailable. ErrTmuxKillFailed means the agent process still runs: retry later. After a sent kill, ErrTmuxUnresponsive or ErrTmuxNotAvailable means the kill may or may not have taken effect: check again later. "A finished row's own old session" in agent-director's docs/operator-actions.md describes every case. Its ad.kill.called trail record carries include_finished true. Run it as the agents' user and in their tmux environment. An error prints one JSON envelope ({err_name, err_description}) on stderr and exits 1.

### Flags

- `--instance-id <id>`: Id of the finished row. Required.

### Output

{"kill_sent": true} or {"kill_sent": false}: kill_sent is true exactly when a pane or session kill was sent.

## delete

`agent-director-admin delete --instance-id <id> [--instance-id <id>...]`

Remove rows by id, bypassing every guard: the human's repair tool for a row nothing else removes, such as a row whose recorded tmux session name cannot be used, which resume and reuse refuse and expire keeps. It also removes each row's permission requests, session history and subagent records and clears it as the parent of any other row. It touches no tmux session and no transcript: on a live row the agent keeps running, untracked. Never remove a row after a kill that did not succeed. Each id is processed on its own; a failure on one never aborts the batch. Run it as the agents' user and in their tmux environment. An error prints one JSON envelope ({err_name, err_description}) on stderr and exits 1.

### Flags

- `--instance-id <id>`: Id of a row to remove. Repeatable; at least one is required.

### Output

{"results": {...}}, mapping each requested id to "ok" when the row was removed, "ErrSpawnNotFound" when no row has the id, or "ErrInternal" on any other store failure.

## help

`agent-director-admin help`

Print the help of every verb and the global flags. agent-director-admin with no verb, --help and -h print it too, and every verb's --help or -h prints that verb's help. It opens no store and loads no config.

### Flags

_None._

### Output

Plain text, opening with the human-approval statement.

## version

`agent-director-admin version`

Print the build-time version stamp and config_dir, as agent-director version does; install.sh installs the two binaries only when their stamps (version and commit) are the same. agent-director-admin --version and -v print it too. It opens no store and loads no config. An error prints one JSON envelope ({err_name, err_description}) on stderr and exits 1.

### Flags

_None._

### Output

{"version": "...", "commit": "...", "config_dir": "..."}: the version stamp, the full git SHA the binary was built from and the directory it keeps its files in (~/.config/agent-director).
